sources.title: Emergency numbers in Ghana (112 national emergency line)
sources.publisher: National Communications Authority / Ministry of the Interior
sources.rights: Factual public-safety information; Government of Ghana publications

renderings.title: Emergency telephone numbers
renderings.summary: Call 112 for any emergency in Ghana. You can also call 191 for police, 192 for fire service and 193 for ambulance.
renderings.body:
Ghana's national emergency number is 112. It works from any mobile network and connects you to police, fire or ambulance services.

Direct lines:
- Police: 191
- Fire Service: 192
- Ambulance (National Ambulance Service): 193

When you call, say where you are, what has happened and how many people need help. Stay on the line until the operator tells you to hang up.

renderings.title: Ɔhaw a ɛyɛ den ho telefon nɔma
renderings.summary: Frɛ 112 sɛ ɔhaw kɛse bi asi. Wobɛtumi afrɛ 191 ama polisi, 192 ama ogya adwumakuo, 193 ama ambulance.
renderings.body:
Ghana ɔman no ɔhaw nɔma ne 112. Ɛyɛ adwuma wɔ network biara so.

- Polisi: 191
- Ogya adwumakuo: 192
- Ambulance: 193

Sɛ wofrɛ a, ka baabi a wowɔ, nea asi, ne nnipa dodow a wɔhia mmoa.

renderings.body:
Ghana ɔman no ɔhaw nɔma ne 112. Ɛyɛ adwuma wɔ network biara so.

renderings.title: Xaxa me kaƒoƒo xexlẽmewo
renderings.summary: Yɔ 112 ne xaxa aɖe le edzi yim le Ghana. Àte ŋu ayɔ 191 na kpovitɔwo, 192 na dzotsilawo, 193 na ambulance.
renderings.body:
Ghana dukɔa ƒe xaxa me xexlẽme enye 112. Ewɔa dɔ le network ɖe sia ɖe dzi.

- Kpovitɔwo: 191
- Dzotsilawo: 192
- Ambulance: 193

Ne èyɔ la, gblɔ afi si nèle, nu si dzɔ, kple ame nenie hiã kpekpeɖeŋu.

renderings.title: Oshara mli tsɛmɔ nɔmbai
renderings.summary: Tsɛ 112 kɛ oshara ko ba yɛ Ghana. Obaanyɛ otsɛ 191 kɛha polisi, 192 kɛha la tsuji, 193 kɛha ambulance.
renderings.body:
Ghana maŋ lɛ oshara nɔmba ji 112. Etsuɔ nii yɛ network fɛɛ nɔ.

- Polisi: 191
- La tsuji: 192
- Ambulance: 193

Kɛ otsɛ lɛ, kɛɛ he ni oyɔɔ, nɔ ni ba, kɛ mɛi abɔ ni hiɔ yelikɛbuamɔ.

sources.title: Ghana Card registration requirements
sources.rights: Public information from a Government of Ghana agency; summarised in editors' own words

renderings.title: How to register for the Ghana Card
renderings.summary: Register for the Ghana Card at a National Identification Authority (NIA) office. Bring proof of Ghanaian citizenship such as a birth certificate or passport, or a relative who already holds a Ghana Card to vouch for you.
renderings.body:
The Ghana Card is the national identity card issued by the National Identification Authority (NIA). It is needed for many services including SIM registration, opening a bank account and NHIS enrolment.

To register:
1. Go to an NIA registration centre or district office.
2. Bring one of: a Ghanaian birth certificate, a valid Ghanaian passport, or a citizenship certificate. If you have none, a parent or relative who already has a Ghana Card may vouch for you at the centre.
3. Your photograph, fingerprints and details are captured. You receive a slip and are told when and where to collect the card.

First-time registration for Ghanaian citizens has been free at NIA offices; replacement cards and premium services attract fees. Fees and requirements can change, so confirm with your NIA district office.

renderings.title: Sɛnea wobɛkyerɛw wo din agye Ghana Card
renderings.summary: Kɔ NIA ɔfese bi na kyerɛw wo din gye Ghana Card. Fa awo krataa anaa passport kɔ, anaa wo busuani a ɔwɔ Ghana Card dedaw nka ho asɛm ma wo.
renderings.body:
Ghana Card yɛ ɔman no nnipa nkyerɛkyerɛmu krataa a National Identification Authority (NIA) de ma. Wohia no ama SIM card, sikakorabea, ne NHIS.

1. Kɔ NIA ɔfese a ɛbɛn wo.
2. Fa awo krataa, Ghana passport, anaa ɔmanni krataa kɔ. Sɛ wunni biara a, wo busuani a ɔwɔ Ghana Card betumi adi wo adanse.
3. Wɔbɛfa wo mfonini ne wo nsateaa. Wɔbɛkyerɛ wo bere a wobɛkɔ akogye card no.

Nsɛm yi betumi asesa; bisa NIA ɔfese a ɛbɛn wo.

sources.title: Voter registration eligibility and process
sources.rights: Public information from a Government of Ghana body; summarised

renderings.title: Registering to vote
renderings.summary: Ghanaian citizens aged 18 or older can register to vote at an Electoral Commission registration centre during an announced registration period. Bring your Ghana Card or Ghanaian passport.
renderings.body:
You can register as a voter if you are a Ghanaian citizen, are 18 years or older, and are of sound mind.

The Electoral Commission (EC) announces registration periods before elections and opens centres in every district. Bring a Ghana Card or valid Ghanaian passport. The EC has also allowed registered voters to vouch for applicants without documents, subject to its rules at the time.

After registering you receive a voter ID card. Check your name on the provisional voters' register when it is exhibited, and report any errors at your district EC office.

sources.title: How to register and renew NHIS membership
sources.rights: Public information from a Government of Ghana authority; summarised

renderings.title: Joining or renewing the National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS)
renderings.summary: Register for NHIS at any NHIS district office with your Ghana Card, or renew by dialling *929# on your mobile phone. Children, people aged 70 and above, pregnant women and the very poor are exempt from the premium.
renderings.body:
The National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS) covers most common illnesses at accredited facilities.

New registration: visit an NHIS district office with your Ghana Card. Your details and photo are captured and you pay a premium and processing fee unless you are exempt.

Renewal: dial *929# from your mobile phone and follow the prompts, or use the NHIS mobile app, or visit an office.

Exempt groups (no premium): children under 18, persons aged 70 and above, pregnant women, SSNIT pensioners, and persons classified as indigent. Fees and rules change, so confirm at your district office.

renderings.title: NHIS me gegeɖeɖe alo eƒe yeyewɔwɔ
renderings.summary: Yi NHIS ƒe nutome ɔfis kple wò Ghana Card nàŋlɔ ŋkɔ, alo ƒo *929# le wò kaƒomɔ dzi nàwɔe yeye. Ðeviwo, ame siwo xɔ ƒe 70 kple edzi, funɔwo kple ame dahewo mexea fe o.
renderings.body:
NHIS xea dɔléle geɖewo ƒe fe le kɔdzi siwo woɖe mɔ na.

Ŋkɔŋɔŋlɔ yeye: yi NHIS ɔfis kple wò Ghana Card.
Yeyewɔwɔ: ƒo *929# le wò kaƒomɔ dzi.

Ame siwo mexea fe o: ɖevi siwo mexɔ ƒe 18 o, ame siwo xɔ ƒe 70 kple edzi, funɔwo, SSNIT pensiɔn xɔlawo kple ame dahewo. Sewo ate ŋu atrɔ; bia wò nutome ɔfis.

sources.title: Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 2020 (Act 1027) and registry guidance
sources.rights: Ghanaian legislation and public guidance; summarised

escalation.label: Births and Deaths Registry district office

renderings.title: Registering a child's birth
renderings.summary: Register a birth at the Births and Deaths Registry office in your district, ideally within the first 12 months when registration is free. Bring the hospital weighing card or birth notification and a parent's ID.
renderings.body:
Every birth in Ghana should be registered with the Births and Deaths Registry. A birth certificate is needed for school enrolment, the Ghana Card and a passport.

How to register:
1. Go to the Registry office in the district where the child was born.
2. Bring the child health record (weighing card) or hospital birth notification, and the Ghana Card or other ID of a parent.
3. Provide the child's names, date and place of birth, and parents' details.

Registration within the first 12 months is free. Late registration is still possible but attracts a fee and may require extra documents. Confirm current requirements at your district office.

sources.title: Ghana passport online application
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Regional Integration, Passport Office
sources.rights: Public information from a Government of Ghana ministry; summarised

renderings.title: Applying for a Ghanaian passport
renderings.summary: Apply for a passport online at the Passport Office website, pay the fee, then attend your chosen Passport Application Centre with your Ghana Card and supporting documents for biometric capture.
renderings.body:
Ghanaian passports are issued by the Passport Office of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Steps:
1. Complete the application online at passport.mfa.gov.gh and pay the fee.
2. Print the form and book an appointment at a Passport Application Centre.
3. Attend with your Ghana Card, birth certificate and any other required documents. Your photo and fingerprints are taken.
4. Collect the passport when notified; standard and expedited processing times differ.

Fees and document requirements change from time to time; check the official website before you apply.
